source.title: Activation Steering for Masked Diffusion Language Models
source.authors: Adi Shnaidman; Erin Feiglin; Osher Yaari; Efrat Mentel; Amit Levi; R. Lapid

record.tranche_reason: The study adapts the harmful-minus-harmless mean-activation direction and projection-based removal procedure to masked diffusion models, then measures refusal and safety outcomes.
record.gate_note: The validation heatmaps are used to select a layer-token direction, so their values are not recorded as results. GCG, PAIR, and Slice are comparison baselines, not tests of the direction itself; their results are not included as rows. The paper reports no harmless-request refusal-induction test or general-capability evaluation.
record.test_reason: Applies the harmful-minus-harmless mean-difference direction and Arditi-style projection ablation to masked diffusion LMs, a new architecture. It measures keyword refusal and LLaMA Guard 2 safety on held-out JailbreakBench prompts against unsteered direct prompting.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors also claim refusal in MDLMs is governed by an approximately one-dimensional direction, and that pre-instruction-token directions work as well as post-instruction ones, unlike in autoregressive models. They read the null Llama-3 result as evidence that safety representations are architecture-dependent.
record.recipe_differences: Uses harmful-minus-harmless mean activations and projection-based direction removal, adapted to MDLMs. It selects a layer-token source on validation data and applies the selected direction globally during reverse diffusion. It does not test direction addition.
record.method_sensitivity: Effect varies by MDLM, source token position, token scope, layer range, and denoising-step schedule. The paper also reports different outcomes for cross-lingual versus cross-architecture transfer.

fits_no_version.finding: A LLaDA-extracted direction applied to Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct produces no measurable change in refusal or safety.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Refusal directions do not transfer between independently trained models of different architectures without alignment of their representation spaces.

record.peer_reviewed: Accepted as a workshop paper at ReALM-GEN, ICLR 2026
record.problems: The harmful training prompts are filtered to retain instructions that the model already refuses. Evaluation uses 100 JailbreakBench harmful prompts and binary keyword matching plus LLaMA Guard 2; no uncertainty estimates are reported. The study does not evaluate harmless-request refusal induction or preservation of general capabilities.
record.rows_left_out: Validation-set layer-token heatmaps are used for selecting the direction and are excluded. Figure 4's individual κ points and Figure 6b's other plotted layer ranges are not separately extracted; the text summarizes the relevant trends in r37-r40 and selected layer ranges in r25-r36.

untested.parts: Adding the direction to induce refusal on harmless prompts; preservation of general capabilities after ablation; any harmless-prompt evaluation.
Transfer between LLaDA variants (separate directions were extracted per model) and base-to-instruct transfer.

missing.what: Numeric bar values for the token-scope and layer-range ablations (e.g., unsteered ~99/97, all tokens ~12/1, layer 23 only, late 25–32) are printed in the figure but not recorded.

Validation heatmaps show pre-instruction token positions as effective as post-instruction ones, and LLaDA-8B and LLaDA-1.5 share sensitivity regions. These are selection data, but the paper presents the pre-instruction result as a diffusion-specific departure from the original last-token recipe; test-set rows r1/r5/r9 partly cover it.

record.verdict_notes: The single-direction ablation largely holds in LLaDA MDLMs. The study tests only the removal half of V1, with no capability check and no harmless-prompt control, and the harmful training prompts were filtered to ones the model refuses. The GCG, PAIR and Slice baselines are correctly excluded. The cross-architecture null should not count against V6: applying another model's vector to an unrelated residual space is not expected to work. The scope ablations bear on how the intervention must be applied in diffusion models, not on whether the direction mediates refusal.

versions.untested_parts: Tests projection-based removal on harmful prompts. Does not test adding the direction to induce refusal on harmless requests or whether other general abilities are largely preserved.
No weight-edit or released-model abliteration experiment.
Does not test whether attacks suppress the refusal direction or whether training against its ablation improves robustness.
Uses a selected single direction but does not compare it with affine, cone, or multiple-direction accounts.
Measures refusal and safety with separate metrics, but does not test whether harmfulness judgment is encoded separately from the refusal decision.
Tests English-Chinese transfer within LLaDA-8B-Instruct and transfer from that model to Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct. Does not test transfer between the MDLM variants or from base to instruct models.
Does not vary refusal-training method, data, or timing.
Does not identify or evaluate a model that reasons before answering as a reasoning-model test.

tranche.reason: It uses Arditi's recipe and measures (128/128 diff-in-means, validation selection, all-layer projection, 100 JailbreakBench prompts, substrings plus LLaMA Guard 2), but on masked diffusion LMs with adapted token sites and per-denoising-step application. That is a new setting with a result on the claim. T1 would also be defensible.

source_check.notes: The Llama-3-8B-Instruct null applies an LLaDA direction to an unrelated model (text only, no numbers), so it is not a V6 test and shouldn't count against V6. There is no random-direction control, capability check or activation-addition test. Section 4.1 prose says LLaDA keyword refusal fell to '0%–16%', but Table 1 gives 0–7 for LLaDA (16 is MMaDA). Figure 6a/6b bar labels survive in the text but their mapping to conditions is lost.

statements.correction: MMaDA-8B-MixCoT, JailbreakBench n=100: keyword refusal 26.0→12.0 (pre-instruction) / 16.0 (post-instruction); LLaMA Guard 2 safety 50.0→25.0 / 31.0 (falls). No StrongREJECT. The validation heatmap shows broadly degraded safety with no well-defined layer–token localization; the authors call the drop a 'further, consistent degradation in safety'.
statements.problem: 'LLaMA Guard 2 safety rises 14.3%→22.0%' and 'StrongREJECT 0.45→0.29' are not in this study; LG safety falls here and StrongREJECT isn't measured. The authors don't attribute the weaker MMaDA effect to diffuse localization.

statements.correction: LLaDA-8B-Instruct, Appendix A.2 Fig 6a: input-only steering clearly reduces keyword refusal and LG safety (authors: majority of the effect); output-only gives little to no change; all-token steering is strongest.
statements.problem: 'Input-token-only projection works' overstates. It gives a clear but incomplete reduction (the record rates r19/r20 partial), and the result is from one model only.

Minor: 'with controls' means only unsteered and jailbreak baselines; there is no random-direction control. The EN→ZH Direct baseline (97/99) equals Table 1's English values, and the text doesn't say it was measured on Chinese prompts.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: LLaDA models, harmful prompts, keyword-refusal metric
reader_labels.reason: Projection reduces keyword-refusal scores from 97.0% to 0.0% or 4.0% in LLaDA-8B-Instruct and from 98.0% to 6.0% or 7.0% in LLaDA-1.5 (r1, r3, r5, r7).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: Safety scores remain above zero after steering, and the refusal reduction is smaller in MMaDA than in the LLaDA models (r2, r4, r6, r8, r9, r10, r11, r12).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Restricted token, layer, and denoising-step interventions
reader_labels.reason: Effects depend on intervention scope: output-only and early-layer restrictions have little effect, while broader and early-step interventions work better (r19-r40).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: Directions selected in one language substantially lower both refusal and safety scores when applied in the other language (r13-r16).

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.reason: The transferred direction produces no measurable change in refusal or safety scores (r17, r18).
